Conduct the superlet transform on a time series or signal

Source: R/analyse_superlet.R, R/zzz_aliases_american.R
analyse_superlet.Rd

Compute the superlet transform using a complex Morlet wavelet following the approach of Moca et al. (2021). The superlet transform increases time frequency resolution by combining multiple wavelet orders at each frequency. Both the frequency sampling and the scaling of superlet order with frequency can be explicitly controlled.

Usage

analyse_superlet(
  data,
  upperPeriod,
  lowerPeriod,
  Nf,
  c1,
  o = NULL,
  mult = TRUE,
  order_scaling = c("none", "log2", "linear", "sqrt", "quadratic", "power"),
  order_alpha = 1,
  verbose = FALSE,
  detrend = c("linear", "mean", "none"),
  standardize = TRUE,
  run_multicore = FALSE,
  n_cores = NULL,
  standardise = NULL,
  wavelet = "morlet",
  wavelet_order = NULL
)

analyze_superlet(
  data,
  upperPeriod,
  lowerPeriod,
  Nf,
  c1,
  o = NULL,
  mult = TRUE,
  order_scaling = c("none", "log2", "linear", "sqrt", "quadratic", "power"),
  order_alpha = 1,
  verbose = FALSE,
  detrend = c("linear", "mean", "none"),
  standardize = TRUE,
  run_multicore = FALSE,
  n_cores = NULL,
  standardise = NULL,
  wavelet = "morlet",
  wavelet_order = NULL
)

Arguments

data

Input record: a matrix or data frame with depth/time in column 1 and the proxy value in column 2. Rows with NA are removed, the rows are sorted by depth/time and the record is linearly interpolated to the median sampling interval. Required, no default.

upperPeriod

Longest period to analyse, in the same unit as the depth/time column of data (numeric, > lowerPeriod); sets the lowest analysed frequency. Required, no default.

lowerPeriod

Shortest period to analyse, in the same unit as the depth/time column of data (numeric, > 0; at least twice the sampling interval, otherwise a warning is given); sets the highest analysed frequency. Required, no default.

Nf

Number of frequencies of the superlet spectrum (integer, >= 1); the frequencies are spaced evenly in log2 between 1/upperPeriod and 1/lowerPeriod. More frequencies give a finer period axis and a longer computation time. Required, no default.

c1

Base number of cycles of the Morlet wavelet of order 1 (numeric, > 0, typically 2 to 5): the fundamental wavelet width. The wavelets of higher orders have more cycles, see mult. Required, no default.

o

Minimum and maximum superlet order (numeric vector of length 2, values >= 1; fractional orders are allowed and give the last wavelet a fractional weight). The order changes from o[1] at the lowest frequency (longest period) to o[2] at the highest frequency, as set by order_scaling. A single number gives the same order at all frequencies; NULL uses order 1 everywhere (a plain wavelet transform). Default=NULL.

mult

How the number of cycles grows with the order i within a superlet (logical, TRUE or FALSE): TRUE multiplicative (\(c_i = i c_1\)); FALSE additive (\(c_i = c_1 + i - 1\), Moca et al., 2021). Default=TRUE.

order_scaling

How the superlet order increases from o[1] (lowest frequency) to o[2] (highest frequency) (character), one of:

  • "none" or "log2": linear in log2(frequency);

  • "linear": linear in frequency (as in Moca et al., 2021);

  • "sqrt": with the square root of the normalised frequency (fast increase at low frequencies);

  • "quadratic": with the square of the normalised frequency (fast increase at high frequencies);

  • "power": with the normalised frequency to the power order_alpha.

Default="none" (the first element of c("none", "log2", "linear", "sqrt", "quadratic", "power")).

order_alpha

Exponent of the "power" order scaling (numeric, > 0); only used when order_scaling="power". Values greater than 1 keep the order low over most of the frequency range and raise it mainly at the highest frequencies (sharpening the short periods); values smaller than 1 raise it already at low frequencies. Default=1.

verbose

Print the sampling interval to which the record was interpolated and show a progress bar (logical, TRUE or FALSE). Default=FALSE.

detrend

Removal of a trend before the transform (character), one of "linear" (a least-squares linear trend is subtracted), "mean" (the mean is subtracted) or "none". A mean or trend that is not removed leaks into all periods and gives large edge effects, which is a problem for stratigraphic records (for example grey values or counts) that do not have a zero mean. Default="linear" (the first element of c("linear", "mean", "none")).

standardize

Divide the (detrended) record by its standard deviation before the transform (logical, TRUE or FALSE), as in analyse_wavelet, so that the power does not depend on the units of the proxy. Default=TRUE.

run_multicore

Compute the frequencies in parallel on several cores (logical, TRUE or FALSE). Default=FALSE.

n_cores

Number of cores used when run_multicore=TRUE (integer, > 0); NULL picks a safe automatic number (see analyse_wavelet). Results do not depend on the number of cores. Default=NULL.

standardise

British spelling of standardize (logical); if given (not NULL) it overrides standardize. Default=NULL.

wavelet

Mother wavelet (character string or function), given as a name (PyWavelets style names with the order appended, such as "db4", "sym8", "cgau3", "gaus2" or "cmor1.5-1", also work) or as a function psi_hat(omega) that returns the Fourier transform of a user defined mother wavelet. Analytic (complex) wavelets, which give phase and amplitude and can be synchrosqueezed: "morlet" (default; aliases "gabor", "amor"), "morlet0" (exactly zero mean Morlet, admissible for a small omega_nr; alias "morlex"), "paul" (alias "cauchy"), "morse" (generalised Morse wavelet of Olhede and Walden, 2002; aliases "gmw", "airy"), "bump", "cmor" (complex Morlet with bandwidth and centre frequency as in Matlab/PyWavelets), "cgau" (analytic Gaussian derivative; "cmhat" is the complex Mexican hat), "shannon" (complex Shannon, box spectrum), "fbsp" (frequency B-spline), "meyer", "loggabor" (alias "lognormal"), "gammatone" (asymmetric in time: sharp onset, slow decay) and "hann" (raised cosine band). Real wavelets, which give a real transform (no phase or envelope): "dog" (derivative of Gaussian; "mexh", "ricker", "marr" and "sombrero" are the Mexican hat, order 2), "morl" (real Morlet), "hhat" (Hermitian hat), "poisson", and the orthogonal wavelets "haar", "db" (Daubechies), "sym" (Symlets) and "battle" (Battle-Lemarie spline wavelets), which are computed in the frequency domain from their filters. The period axis of the orthogonal wavelets is approximate because their spectra are broad and not symmetric. A narrow wavelet (Paul, low-order DOG, Shannon, Haar) resolves position well, a wide one (Morse with a large beta, Morlet with a high omega_nr, bump) resolves period well. Default="morlet".

wavelet_order

Parameter(s) of the wavelet (see analyse_wavelet); when it is NULL the wavelet with the same relative bandwidth as a Morlet wavelet with the superlet cycles is used at every frequency (cycles are converted as omega_0 = 2 pi cycles / 5). Parameters: paul: order m (default 4); dog: derivative m (default 2); morse: c(gamma, beta) or beta alone with gamma = 3 (default c(3, 20)); bump: c(mu, sigma) (default c(5, 0.6)); cmor: c(bandwidth, centre frequency) (default c(1.5, 1)); cgau: derivative m (default 4); shannon: c(bandwidth, centre frequency) (default c(2, 1.5)); fbsp: c(m, bandwidth, centre frequency) (default c(2, 2, 1.5)); loggabor: c(centre angular frequency, log-width) (default c(6, 0.25)); meyer and hhat have no parameter; morlet0: omega_0 (default omega_nr); morl: omega_0 (default 5); poisson: order n (default 2); gammatone: c(n, centre angular frequency, bandwidth) (default c(4, 6, 1.5)); hann: c(centre angular frequency, half width) (default c(6, 3)); db: number of vanishing moments 1 to 20 (default 4, "haar" = "db1"); sym: 2 to 20 (default 8); battle: spline order 1, 3, 5 or 7 (default 3). For the Morlet wavelet the number of cycles is set by c1, o and mult. Default=NULL.

Value

A list with class "analyze.superlet" containing Power: time frequency power spectrum dt: sampling interval after interpolation dj: number of frequencies Power.avg: average spectral power Period: physical periods corresponding to frequencies nc: number of columns in the input data nr: number of frequency levels axis.1: x axis values (time or depth) axis.2: y axis values (log2 scaled periods) c1: base number of wavelet cycles o: numeric vector of length two defining the minimum and maximum superlet order. If NULL, all frequencies are analysed using order one. freq.scale: scaling of the frequencies order.mode: order.mode ("none", "log2", "linear", "sqrt", "power") order: superlet order of every period coi: distance from the start and end of the record within which edge effects are important (cone of influence), for every period coi.1, coi.2: the cone of influence as polygons (x and log2 period), drawn by the plot functions x: interpolated x values y: interpolated signal values

References

Moca, V. V., Bârzan, H., Nagy-Dăbâcan, A., & Mureșan, R. C. (2021). Time-frequency super-resolution with superlets. Nature Communications, 12(1), 337. doi:10.1038/s41467-020-20539-9

Author

Adapted from MATLAB implementations by V. V. Moca et al. (2021)

Examples

# \donttest{
## Example 1. Using the Total Solar Irradiance data set of Steinhilber et al. (2012)
TSI_sl <-
  analyse_superlet(
    data = TSI,
    upperPeriod = 8192,
    lowerPeriod = 16,
    Nf = 20,
    c1 = 2,
    o = c(1, 5),
    mult = TRUE,
    order_scaling = "log2",
    order_alpha = 1,
    verbose = FALSE
  )
#> Warning: lowerPeriod is shorter than twice the sampling interval (44): periods below the Nyquist period cannot be resolved


## Example 2. Using the magnetic susceptibility data set of Pas et al. (2018)
mag_sl <-
  analyse_superlet(
    data = mag,
    upperPeriod = 254,
    lowerPeriod = 0.1,
    Nf = 20,
    c1 = 2,
    o = c(1, 5),
    mult = TRUE,
    order_scaling = "log2",
    order_alpha = 1,
    verbose = FALSE
  )


## Example 3. Using the greyscale data set of Zeeden et al. (2013)
grey_sl <-
  analyse_superlet(
    data = grey,
    upperPeriod = 256,
    lowerPeriod = 0.02,
    Nf = 20,
    c1 = 2,
    o = c(2,5),
    mult = TRUE,
    order_scaling = "log2",
    order_alpha = 1,
    verbose = FALSE)
# }
